issues.description: The Bitmap24::save method has conflicting return types between the header and its implementation in the template repository: the header declares int save(const std::string&), while the .cpp defines void Bitmap24::save(const std::string&). This mismatch will cause compilation/linking errors and confuses students about the correct API. The solution repository uses void, which aligns with the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration and definition consistent. Change the template header to match the implementation/solution by declaring: void save(const std::string &i_filename); (or alternatively change the .cpp to return int and provide a return value). Prefer updating the header to void to match the implementation and the solution repository.

issues.description: The member function Bitmap24::save is declared with a different return type in the template header than in its implementation and the solution header. In example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp (template) save(...) is declared to return int, but example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp (template) defines Bitmap24::save(...) with return type void. The solution repository's example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares save(...) as void. This mismatch (header vs. implementation and template vs. solution) creates confusion about the intended signature of the same conceptual entity (the bitmap save method) and may lead students to compile/link/runtime surprises.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the declaration and implementation of Bitmap24::save to the same return type. Change the template header declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'int save(const std::string &i_filename);' to 'void save(const std::string &i_filename);' so it matches the implementation and the solution header.
